hub_alone: Hub “{name}” · not linked to other hubs
machine: This computer is “{name}” on the hub
awaiting_title: Confirm this computer on your phone
awaiting_hint: In the phone app, tap “It's mine”
node_offline_title: Persona's background service isn't running on this computer
node_offline_hint: Connected to the hub, but it can't use this computer. Click Restart background service below.
node_waiting: The hub is reaching this computer's node…
unpaired_title: Not connected to a hub yet
unpaired_hint: Get a pairing link from Add computer on your phone or the web, then click Paste pairing link… or just open the link
refused_default: The hub doesn't accept this computer's credentials. Pair again.
passive_unpaired: Listening for a hub to pair
passive_code_left: The pairing link is good for {left}. Paste it in the hub's admin page under Computers › Add computer › Hub connects
passive_code_hint: Click Pair or change connection… to make a pairing link for the hub
passive_node_offline: The hub connected, but this computer's node isn't running
service_missing_hint: Click Install background service. It starts when you sign in to Windows and keeps this computer connected.
link_not_running_hint: The background service restarts it within seconds. If this stays, click Restart background service.
notify_awaiting_title: Confirm this computer on your phone
notify_awaiting_body: The hub is waiting for you to tap “It's mine” in the phone app.
notify_offline_body: Couldn't reach the hub for a minute. Still trying.
notice_other_app: This link is for the phone or desktop app, not for pairing this computer. Copy this computer's pairing link from Add computer on your phone or the web.
notice_incomplete: This pairing link is incomplete (no token). Copy it again from Add computer on your phone or the web.
preview_no_hub: The link doesn't say where the hub is
preview_pinned: Pinned: connects only to the hub that made this link
preview_machine: This computer will be “{name}” on the hub
passive_paired: Paired with a hub. If you make a new link and pair another hub, the current one can no longer connect.
passive_paired_named: Paired with hub “{hub}”. If you make a new link and pair another hub, it can no longer connect.
switch_to_active: The hub connects to this computer now. Active mode is still paired; no need to pair again.
switch_to_passive: This computer connects to the hub now. Passive mode is still paired; no need to pair again.
active_intro: Copy the pairing link from Add computer on your phone or the web and paste it here (or just open the link). It works once, within 10 minutes.
machine_placeholder: Machine ID (not needed if the link has one)
addresses_hint: Tried in this order. The hub updates this list once connected.
addresses_trust: Via reverse proxy · system certificates: checked against the system's trusted CAs and the domain name; the hub's key isn't pinned
addresses_empty: None yet. They come from the link and the hub once paired.
passive_title: Let the hub connect to this computer
passive_intro: This computer listens on a port, and the hub connects using the fingerprint it got when pairing. Use it for computers the hub can reach directly, like desktops or servers with a fixed address. A laptop that changes networks can't be reached; choose This computer connects instead.
code_intro: Paste this link in the hub's admin page under Computers › Add computer › Hub connects. It works once, within 10 minutes:
code_addrs: The hub tries these addresses in order: {addrs}. If it can't reach any of them, change the address in the hub's admin page.
firewall_hint: Firewall: open this port to the hub only, not to everyone. In an administrator PowerShell, run this line with <hub-address> replaced by the hub's address:
firewall_proxy: If the hub connects through a proxy, allow the proxy's address instead.
paired_ok: Paired: this computer is “{name}” on the hub
no_webview: WebView2 Runtime is missing, so only the right-click menu works. Install Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime and open this again.
error_no_service: The background service isn't installed: click Install background service first.
error_install_in_terminal: Can't install from here: run persona-link install in a terminal.
error_pair_unreachable:
Can't reach the hub ({hosts}). Check that it's running, that the address is right and that this computer is online, then try again.
(Details: {detail})
error_pair_rejected:
The hub doesn't accept this pairing link (it expired, was already used or was revoked). Get a new one from Add computer and paste it here.
(Details: {detail})
rename_hint: Shown in the app, on the web and on the admin page. The computer's id stays the same.
renamed_ok: This computer is now “{name}” on the hub
ssh_intro: Reach the hub through an SSH server using this computer's ssh client, keys and ~/.ssh/config.
ssh_target_label: Hub address as that server sees it
ssh_always_hint: When off, direct hub addresses are tried first and SSH is used only if they fail.
ssh_test_ok: SSH tunnel reached the hub at {target}.
ssh_error_no_ssh: There is no ssh command on this computer; install an OpenSSH client first.
ssh_error_auth_refused: The SSH server ({server}) refused authentication; check your key, ssh-agent, or ~/.ssh/config.
ssh_error_host_key: This SSH server's host key isn't trusted yet; run “{cmd}” once in a terminal to check and accept it.
ssh_error_forward_refused: The SSH server refused port forwarding to {target}; check AllowTcpForwarding and permitopen on the server.
ssh_error_target_unreachable: The hub isn't answering at {target} through the SSH server; check that the hub is running and the target port is right.
ssh_error_ssh_unreachable: Can't reach the SSH server ({server}); check the server address and this computer's network.
ssh_error_invalid: Enter an SSH server as [user@]host[:port] or an alias, and a target as host:port.
